goal: Implement the unattended batch run state machine defined by docs/specs/unattended-initiative-batch-run.spec.md sections 3.4 and 4: a single serial driver that owns every batch and child state transition, drives each child through the existing Kernel obligations without inventing authority, parks human-owned work and skips its dependent subtree, honors budget, deadline, and expiry stop conditions, persists recoverable state, and writes exactly one run report.

acceptance.assertion: startBatch drives children strictly serially through prepared, running, and one terminal batch state of completed, budget_stopped, failed, or rejected, with per-child states pending, enrolled, settled, committed, needs_human, and skipped_blocked. Every transition of this machine lives in runtime/unattended and runtime/kernel/batch_authority.ts; no Host adapter module writes batch state or advances a child, and the driver imports no Host adapter module. Each child is enrolled through the batch-derived capability and then advanced only through the existing Kernel obligation surface, so implementation, freeze, deterministic QA, and Review evidence remain Kernel-owned and the driver never fabricates a QA pass, a Review verdict, or a settlement. A child that returns a user-owned obligation of resolve_user_decision, a breaking revise_intent, a blocking finding, or record-user-approval, and a child that reaches the consecutive QA failure limit, are parked as needs_human, and every transitive dependent of a parked or failed child becomes skipped_blocked and is never enrolled.

Budget exhaustion through max_children, deadline_at, or authorization expiry terminates the batch as budget_stopped, which is an intentional stop and not a failure, and reaching it never marks a completed child as failed. Expiry and deadline block only the enrollment of a new child: a child already enrolled runs to its own Kernel terminal settlement and its commit, so no unsettled claim, orphaned workspace claim, or uncommitted working tree is left behind. Batch run state is persisted at .imm/state/batches/<batch_id>.json through the existing kernel store lock and is Git-ignored; after an interruption the driver reconstructs the exact pending obligation from that state plus a fresh Kernel projection, never replays a committed mutation, and refuses to resume an expired authorization, requiring a new literal-user confirmation. Exactly one run report is written after the final child settles or the batch stops, naming the terminal batch state, each child's terminal state and reason, the commits created, and the single next action.
